summary: This is a fragment of a Maven pom.xml file, not Java code. It adds Mockito to the project so that tests can create stand-in (mock) objects for collaborators like the TemperatureSensor interface, instead of talking to real hardware.

lines.text: Maven keeps every external library the project relies on inside this one block, so adding a library means adding an entry here rather than hunting down a JAR file yourself.
The comment marks the JUnit 5 entry that is already present from earlier in the chapter; Mockito is added alongside it, not in place of it, because you still need JUnit to run the tests.
The groupId and artifactId together are the library's coordinates, and mockito-core is the part of Mockito that provides mock(), when(), and verify().
Pinning an exact version means the build behaves the same on every machine today and a year from now, instead of silently picking up a newer release.
The test scope keeps Mockito on the classpath only while compiling and running tests, so a mocking framework never ships inside your production application.
